page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The instance provides 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with a dedicated 1:1 core-to-thread allocation. Its cache hierarchy consists of 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, allocating 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The configuration includes 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without bundled local storage, and includes no discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results show exceptional memory subsystem performance. The r8gn.8xlarge registers uncached large-block read bandwidth of 414.89 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 186.46 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10% tier. PassMark memory and database operation tests also reach top-tier rankings at 3,396.37 and 47,350.52 respectively. Multi-core compute performance is robust, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,290.0 and Clang compilation scores of 47,583.0. In network-facing benchmarks, the server delivers Redis SET throughput of 67.03 million operations per second and 72.48 GB/sec in static web serving. In contrast, single-core CPU metrics and heavy LLM prompt processing exhibit average to lower-tier results.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides favorable resource density for memory-bound applications without paying for unnecessary compute capacity. Because local storage is absent, storage throughput relies entirely on remote EBS volumes over the dedicated network architecture. Workloads best aligned with the r8gn.8xlarge include in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-concurrency relational database management systems, large-scale Clang build pipelines, and high-throughput web service layers.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated arm64 cores running AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processors at 2.8 GHz. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it provisions 256.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The instance lacks local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on remote EBS block storage and a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier performance in uncached memory bandwidth, PassMark database operations, and Geekbench multi-core workloads, alongside strong throughput in Redis SET operations and Clang compilation. Single-core processing and large-parameter language model inference register in average or lower tiers. Given its large memory capacity and dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores, the r8gn.8xlarge is well suited for memory-intensive architectures, including in-memory datastores, distributed caching tiers, analytics data processing, and large software build fleets.
